jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Life Sciences Research (Genetic Medicine)
jobs.location: Boston, MA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Thousands of rare genetic diseases have a known cause but no approved treatment. Advances in gene editing and oligonucleotide medicines have made it possible to design therapies for very small populations, sometimes for a single patient, but developing them remains slow and costly. Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is exploring how frontier AI, combined with deep drug development expertise and strong external partnerships, can help change that.

We’re hiring a Technical Program Manager to bring structure and momentum to this work. You’ll coordinate across programs that support the development of individualized genetic medicines, advance research into new therapeutic approaches, and help patient organizations, non-profits, and researchers use Claude in their own rare disease work. You’ll partner closely with scientists, engineers, clinicians, and external collaborators to keep complex efforts moving toward shared milestones.

Much of this work remains in early stages, so this is a foundational role on a small team. You’ll help define how the team operates, build the plans and processes that allow it to grow, and work with our researchers and engineers to find where Claude can be most useful.

If you’ve run complex programs in drug development or clinical research and want to help advance treatments for rare disease, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and own an integrated program plan, including milestones, dependencies, risks, budgets, and key decisions
  • Coordinate with clinical, manufacturing, and research partners on programs that span preclinical development, manufacturing, regulatory review, and clinical care
  • Run the operating cadence with external partners, tracking progress and raising risks early
  • Work with Legal, Finance, and Partnerships to turn agreements into clear operating plans and track commitments
  • Coordinate research across internal scientists, academic collaborators, companies, and contract research organizations, helping to scope projects, sequence work, and support timely decisions
  • Help ensure that data is shared responsibly and in a usable form, with appropriate consent, privacy protections, and data-sharing agreements in place
  • Lead programs that support non-profits, patient organizations, and academic and independent researchers, from onboarding through ongoing support and feedback
  • Help connect genetic diagnosis efforts with therapeutic research and development
  • Share insights from partners and programs with Anthropic’s research and product teams to help improve Claude for scientific and medical research
  • Write clear status updates, risk assessments, and decision memos, and build processes that scale with the team

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience as a technical program manager or program lead on complex drug development, clinical research, or translational science programs involving multiple external organizations, such as manufacturers, contract research organizations, or clinical sites
  • Working knowledge of how a therapy moves from preclinical development into the clinic, including manufacturing, regulatory filings, and clinical operations, and how a delay in one stage affects the others
  • Scientific fluency in molecular biology or genetics, sufficient to follow experimental plans, review data with scientists, and understand tradeoffs
  • Strong program management skills, including project planning, milestones, risk registers, budget tracking, and dependency management across many concurrent workstreams
  • A track record of driving work to completion across organizations without formal authority
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to make complex scientific and operational issues easy to understand and act on
  • Comfort working with ambiguity and building process where none exists
  • Excitement about Anthropic’s mission to build safe and beneficial AI

Preferred qualifications

  • An advanced degree in a life science, engineering, or related field
  • Experience with gene therapy, gene editing, or oligonucleotide programs, especially individualized (N-of-1) or ultra-rare disease programs
  • Clinical operations experience, such as multi-site trials, master protocols, IRB submissions, or site activation
  • Experience managing sponsored research agreements, grants, or philanthropic funding with academic institutions
  • Experience working with patient advocacy groups, rare disease foundations, or other non-profits
  • Familiarity with clinical genomics and genetic diagnosis
  • Experience with patient data governance, including consent, HIPAA, and data-sharing agreements
  • Experience in a role that bridges software or AI and the life sciences
  • Experience as an early hire on a new team, helping define how it operates
  • Hands-on experience using LLM tools like Claude in your day-to-day work

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$290,000—$365,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Engineering Excellence
jobs.location: Livingston, NJ / New York, NY / Sunnyvale, CA / Bellevue, WA
jobs.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About the role:

CoreWeave is seeking a Technical Program Manager to lead programs that level up engineering excellence across our developer teams. In this role, you will own engineering programs that ensure our engineering team can ship fast, without compromising reliability, security or compliance. You will look at the whole software development life cycle (SDLC), get a deep understanding of how our engineers work and what goods look like.  This position is ideal for someone who has run large scale programs across many engineering teams, understands every step of the SDLC  and can keep multi-team execution moving without direct authority.

In this role, TPM will

  • Work closely with our internal developer platform teams to understand the paved path and define engineering excellence.
  • Meet your internal customers, the CoreWeave engineering teams, where they are, understand their priorities and drive their migration onto the paved path. ., 
  • Lead rollout of engineering and security standards across all engineering organizations, including acquired entities, sequencing overlapping changes and managing exceptions.
  • Drive programs that make releases and operations safer, such as change guardrails, progressive rollout, rollback readiness and validation of controls.
  • Partner with platform, infrastructure, security, reliability and observability teams to reduce deployment related incidents and regressions.
  • Create clear visibility into program status, ownership, dependencies, risks, decisions needed and progress against commitments for engineers, product managers and leadership.
  • Work closely with the internal product managers to understand priorities and make outcomes measurable.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in technical program management, infrastructure program management or a similar role in a complex technical environment.
  • Have led complex technical programs spanning developer infrastructure, CI/CD, build and test systems, artifact management, release engineering or distributed systems.
  • Have run large scale migrations or platform adoption programs across many engineering teams, including inventory, wave planning, exception handling and legacy decommission.
  • Can engage deeply with engineers on workflow architecture, deployment systems, rollout risk, observability and operational tradeoffs.
  • Have delivered measurable improvements in developer velocity, deployment throughput, release reliability or engineering efficiency.
  • Know how to turn fragmented ownership and recurring manual work into durable mechanisms, standards and tooling with strong adoption.
  • Use data and qualitative evidence to prioritize work, define useful metrics and distinguish real productivity gains from local optimization.
  • Lead effectively across platform and product teams, resolve ambiguity and keep multi-team execution moving without direct authority.
  • Are Customer obsessed - Treat engineering teams and partners as customers.
  • Communicate with precision and move comfortably between technical detail, operational execution and executive level decisions.
  • Proficiency in JIRA, Confluence and other program management and collaboration tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's or advanced technical degree.
  • Experience with software supply chain security programs such as artifact governance, dependency management, source control hardening or credential and secrets management.
  • Experience integrating acquired companies onto shared engineering platforms and security standards.
  • Experience driving security or compliance driven programs with fixed deadlines across many engineering teams.
  • Experience at a cloud provider, AI infrastructure company, hyperscaler or other high scale technical environment.
  • Comfortable working in a fast moving environment and flexible working with a variety of leadership.

Why CoreWeave

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast!  We’re in an exciting stage of growth, scaling at an unprecedented speed. We are frequently challenging the norm, exploring new technologies and advancing the potential for hyperscale. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our products and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

  • Be Curious at Your Core
  • Act Like an Owner
  • Empower Employees
  • Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
  • Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we continue to grow, opportunities within the organization are evolving and expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. If this resonates with you, come join us!

The base salary range for this role is $157,000 to $210,000. The starting salary will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility). 

What We Offer

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs. The benefits below reflect our US-based offerings for full-time employees; for roles in other locations, benefits vary and are shared during the hiring process. These include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance - 100% paid for by CoreWeave
  • Company-paid Life Insurance 
  • Voluntary supplemental life insurance 
  • Short and long-term disability insurance 
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Health Savings Account
  • Tuition Reimbursement 
  • Ability to Participate in Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
  • Mental Wellness Benefits through Spring Health 
  • Family-Forming support provided by Carrot
  • Paid Parental Leave 
  • Flexible, full-service childcare support with Kinside
  • 401(k) with a generous employer match
  • Flexible PTO
  • Catered lunch each day in our office and data center locations
  • A casual work environment
  • A work culture focused on innovative disruption

California Applicants

California Consumer Privacy Act 

Equal Opportunity & Accommodations

CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace. All qualified applicants and candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information.

As part of this commitment and consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), CoreWeave will ensure that qualified applicants and candidates with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact: careers@coreweave.com.

Export Control Compliance

This position requires access to technology and/or source code subject to U.S. export control laws. Any such access will be provided only in compliance with applicable U.S. export control requirements. As part of the recruitment process, CoreWeave may request limited information reasonably necessary to assess applicable export-control requirements.

Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; work model to confirm. Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. jobs.title: Program Manager - DiscoveryOne
jobs.description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate. The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in agroscience Contract Research Organization services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialized and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products. In over 30 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 58,000 staff across a decentralized and entrepreneurial network of 900 laboratories in over 54 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products. In 2024, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR € 6,515 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years. The Program Manager supports the successful execution of integrated drug discovery programs by providing project planning, coordination, governance, and operational leadership. Working closely with Scientific Project Leaders and cross-functional scientific teams, the Program Manager ensures that program activities remain aligned to agreed timelines, budgets, milestones, and client expectations. The role is responsible for maintaining integrated project plans, facilitating communication across teams and sites, monitoring risks and dependencies, tracking budgets and deliverables, and supporting effective decision-making through clear reporting and governance. The Program Manager serves as a key operational partner to Scientific Project Leaders, enabling efficient program execution and a high-quality client experience. Here's what you'll do: Develop and maintain integrated project plans, timelines, milestones, and action trackers. Coordinate program activities across multidisciplinary scientific teams. Facilitate project meetings and document decisions, actions, risks, and dependencies. Monitor program performance against scope, timelines, budget, and deliverables. Support financial tracking, forecasting, and change management activities. Prepare program reports and dashboards for clients and internal stakeholders. Work closely with Scientific Project Leaders to align operational plans with scientific priorities. Identify and escalate risks, issues, and schedule impacts. Support proposal development, project start-up, and program expansion activities. Contribute to continuous improvement of program management processes and tools. The ideal candidate: Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Chemistry, Biology, Biotechnology, Pharmacy, or a related scientific discipline. A Master's degree is preferred. Typically 1-3 years of project or program management experience in a CRO, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or related drug discovery environment. Experience supporting or managing cross-functional programs involving multiple studies, stakeholders, timelines, budgets, and interdependent deliverables. Working knowledge of integrated drug discovery and the relationship between chemistry, biology, ADME/DMPK, pharmacology, safety, and toxicology activities. Strong program planning and execution skills, including work breakdown, critical-path management, milestone tracking, prioritization, and delivery recovery. Ability to lead cross-functional, matrixed teams through influence, establish clear accountability, and drive timely decisions. Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, revenue and margin awareness, invoicing visibility, and scope control. Working knowledge of risk and issue management, dependency management, change control, governance, and escalation practices. Strong client-facing communication, facilitation, negotiation, stakeholder-management, and presentation skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project-management, collaboration, reporting, and data-visualization tools; experience with Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, SharePoint, CRM, or ERP/AX is desirable. The position is full-time, Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.- 5 p.m., with overtime as needed. What we offer: Excellent full time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, dental, and vision options Life and disability insurance 401(k) with company match Paid vacation and holidays Eurofins USA Discovery Services is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.
